title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF A VLEO SATELLITE TO ENABLE PRECISE ORBITAL MODELLING AND SYSTEM SIZING (ARTES AT 3E.026) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop high fidelity models to allow the mission design of satcom constellations in VLEO. An in-orbit experiment will be designed and manufactured to measure key geographically and time dependent atmospheric parameters (density, radiation, ionospheric, chemical composition etc..) as well as satellite flight parameters (including drag, solar cells efficiency, etc..). These measurements will enable the precise modelling of VLEO systems (incl. orbital mechanics, budgets, system sizing, etc.). Targeted Improvements: Enable precise VLEO orbital mechanics modelling and system sizing.Description: Due to the variability of the atmospheric conditions, the knowledge of environmental and atmospheric data (density, radiation level, chemical composition) is challenging to get, however in-situ measurements are critical to properly design attitude control processing chain. Previous in-orbit experiments have been attempted in the past but have met with limited mission success. Future VLEO satcom constellations are needed to operate for extended periods of time and will need to be resilient to highly variable environments yet providing viable system architecture. The precise orbital mechanics modelling is then crucial for the sizing of the telecommunication systems in VLEO. This in-orbit experiment will gather the relevant data of the orbital space environment in order to generate the flight dynamics modelling required for the AOCS control loop. This will benefit satellites in orbits ranging from 200km-400km, covering VLEO applications. To provide the needed measurements for the atmospheric models, a payload will be designed, including all the necessary sensing instruments. The spacecraft will be launched to a relevant orbit and in situ measurements will be gathered and communicated to ground over the operational lifetime. The key parameters to acquire and process will be: neutral atmosphere density, radiation, chemical composition and ionospheric parameters. In addition to these primary goals, secondary goals suggested by the bidders are invited (e.g. materials resistance to VLEO environment, solar cell ageing, etc.). In designing the experiment, the activity will consider important trade-offs such as:- Single vs multi spacecraft mission profiles- Life extension via on board propulsion- Co- or multi-orbit ISL to improve data latency and data recovery for very low orbits.The activity will allow design, develop or adapt existing payloads,select a host platform, integrate, launch and operate the payloads for the required time, analyse the acquired data, improve the current models and report on the next steps. In addition to the experimental campaign, the activity will include the review and improvement of current available atmospheric models, allowing for modelling improvements through correlation from the gathered in-orbit data. The minimum duration of the flight experiment will be 1 year in order to characterise and measure the atmospheric conditions in VLEO including seasonal atmospheric variability. Footnote: On Delegation Request activities will only be initiated on the explicit request of at least one National Delegation.

title: VERY-LOW MASS-FLOW RATE FLOW CONTROLLER FOR FINE CONTROL FOR GRAVIMETRY MISSIONS - EXPRO PLUS
description: This ITT will allow the Agency to identify the most promising technology for fine mass-flow control of Electric Propulsion systems in order to enhance the efficiency, resolution and minimum thrust step required for Earth Observation gravimetry missions. This activity will assess and benchmark the currently available technologies at concept level and boost the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) to a level of = 3 (analytical and experimental critical function and/or characteristic proof-of-concept),  with the ultimate objective to minimise development risks before entering detailed design, qualification, production and commercialisation phases.The targetof this activity is to design, manufacture, assemble and test a Breadboard Model (BBM) of a flow-rate controller that complies withthe defined requirements. To achieve this goal, several tasks are defined as intermediary objectives which shall be sequentially achieved:-To assess the system/AOCS needs for representative missions, and to extract the relevant propulsion requirements (functional, performance and robustness) -To flow-down the propulsion requirements to mass flow control specification -To survey of available flow control technologies for space and non-space applications-To perform a preliminary benchmark of suitable technologies and selection of most promising technology-To perform numerical simulations and analysis to support design and testing-To design, manufacture and test a prototype-To perform a coupling test with representative thruster (TBC of test facility and thruster to be provided as agency undertaking) for performance verification-To assess the performance improvement with the new development-To define the development roadmap

title: VERIFICATION OF SMALL SATELLITE FITNESS FOR PURPOSE IN NEW APPLICATION DOMAINS - EXPRO+
description: Private investment has stimulated the development of several new small satellite systems within Europe over the last five years. These exploit the reduced technical risk associated with technologies coming from previous ESA and Member State funded developments and benefiting from parallel technology improvements (eg miniaturization, materials etc) so that standard commercial practices can be followed.However, in many cases the privately financed and operated satellites include technical characteristics that create the potential for exploitation in other user domains where there is less acceptance of EO or where technical effort would be required to develop and verify the required information products and services. This may be due to the fact that the sensors are in some way unique or that the the overall system offers unique performance capabilities. Addressing this asymmetric risk structure is routinely practiced within ESA programmes however and given the connections ESA has with a wide range of stakeholders and the experience in supporting diverse EO applications development, ESA is well placed to fund the required developments up to the point where fitness for purpose is demonstrated for a well defined and clearly engaged stakeholder community which can then be the basis for private sector funded follow-on developments and customer engagement. This Invitation to Tender addresses this gap in order to generate an acceptable risk pattern for private sector investors (and the satellite operators) to support the necessary operationalization and commercialization activities. The overall objectives to be achieved are:(i) Accelerate the update of data, information and services from European small satellite operators among customer segments that cannot be effectively addressed by such private sector entities alone(ii) Verify, together with key organizations within the target customer segments, that data, information and services from the small satellite operators address an agreed set of priority issues/gaps and the demonstrated operational performance and processes are consistent with customer segment working practices and are therefore considered to be fit for purposeThis will require the contractor to engage a clear set of customers with requirements that cannot be presently addressed but which could be addressed by modifications to or with a small satellite system currently in operationIdentify a clear set of developments associated with the small satellite system in order to address the requirements of the stakeholders being targeted on a timeframe that is of immediate interest to the target stakeholdersElaborate verification exercises that enable a sufficiently convincing demonstration and verificationthat the developments executed have resulted in the enhanced small satellite system being capable to provide the required information under actual operational conditions to a performance level that is considered acceptable and within working practices that are compliant with the stakeholders operational environment. This should include a clear definition as to what are these threshold performance levels as well as a credible prospect of follow-on commercial uptake if these agreed performance levels are sufficiently well achievedIdentify follow-on mechanisms that can credibly support a transition to full commercial uptake
